en: The Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on the Elder Sukhita,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmabhadra, Imperially Appointed Grand Officer of the Court for Ceremonial Service,
Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and Great Master of Enlightened Teaching, under Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was staying in the city of Kapilavastu together with a great assembly.
At that time, there was a Śākya elder named Sukhavihārin who resided in his own home;
that elder placed deep faith in the Triple Gem.
I take refuge in the Buddha, I take refuge in the Dharma, and I take refuge in the Saṅgha.
Believing solely in the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, I no longer believe in any other non-Buddhist paths.
I seek only the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, and am well-versed in suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.
By seeing the true principle, one obtains a great fruit;
yet it is not that one does not immediately realize bodhi.
At that time, the colors seen by the elder suddenly vanished from view.
At that time, the elder Sukhita, from afar, directed his words toward the World-Honored One, making this aspiration:
"O my Buddha, World-Honored One, endowed with great kindness and great compassion, I pray that you bestow eyes upon me;
bestow the light of the eyes upon me; bestow purity upon my eyes; and remove the darkness and obscurity from my eyes."
Having made this vow, he further spoke these words:
"I now take refuge in the Buddha; I take refuge in the Sugata.
At that time, the World-Honored One, with his pure divine ear which surpasses that of humans, [heard him].
Having heard from afar the words of the vow uttered by that elder,
he immediately addressed the Venerable Ānanda, saying:
"Ānanda, you must now uphold this secret divine mantra of mine."
I shall go to the place of the Śākya elder Subhūti to provide him with rescue, protection, and peace;
and furthermore, I shall bring benefit and happiness to his fourfold assembly as well.
At that time, for the sake of the householder Sukhita and others, the World-Honored One spoke this secret great divine mantra of the Pure Eye:

*Tadyathā* (1) *hiri miri kiri* (2) *hi-he-ta* (3) *hu-yu hu-yu* (4) *hu-ya-vitti* (5) *hu-lu hu-lu hu-lu* (6) *nu nu nu nu lu* (7). By the power of these words of the secret divine mantra of the Pure Eye.
The eyes shall attain purity, removing darkness and eliminating cataracts;
even removing eye diseases caused by wind-poison, yellow-poison,
phlegm-poison, and mucus-poison.
Without pain, without swelling, without affliction, without suffering, and without any discharge or tears—
may all such ailments be entirely eliminated. Furthermore,
through the power of the reality of the precepts, one practices with the power of the reality of asceticism.
The power of reality of the secret mantra of true power; the power of reality of the dependently originated phenomena of true power;
the power of reality of the phenomenon of suffering; the power of reality of the phenomenon of the origin [of suffering];
the power of reality of the phenomenon of cessation; and the power of reality of the phenomenon of the path.
The true power of the srotāpanna; the true power of the sakṛdāgāmin;
the true power of the anāgāmin; the true power of the arhat;
the true power of the pratyekabuddha; and the true power of the bodhisattva.
By the true power of the Buddha, the true power of the Dharma,
and the true power of the Noble Saṅgha— through such powers of truth as these—
the eye attains purity, removing darkness and eliminating obscurations.
All wind-poison eye diseases, bile-poison eye diseases,
phlegm-poison eye diseases, and mucus-poison eye diseases shall be unable to invade [the eyes].
There is no pain, no swelling, no affliction, no suffering, and no discharge of mucus or tears.
The Buddha told Ānanda, "This secret divine mantra was proclaimed together by the six Perfectly Enlightened Ones of the past."
Namely, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Viśvabhū;
the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Krakucchanda;
and the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Kanakamuni.
The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Krakucchanda;
the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Kanakamuni;
and the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Kāśyapa.
I, the seventh Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śākyamuni, now speak in this same way,
even unto the Four Great Heavenly Kings—
namely, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the Heavenly King Who Upholds the Nation, and Virūḍhaka, the Heavenly King Who Increases Growth.
Virūpākṣa, Vaiśravaṇa, Śakra Devānām Indra,
and Mahābrahmā, the Lord of the Sahā World,
all likewise rejoiced and proclaimed it.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"I have not seen those realms of the devas, the realms of Brahmā, nor the realms of the Māras,
nor even the realms of śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, and so forth."
If there is anyone who recites this secret and great divine mantra three times,
whatever illnesses and sufferings may exist that are capable of causing harm, as well as all obscurations and veils,
both internal and external, such as darkness and cataracts— [these shall be eliminated].
...up to diseases caused by devas, diseases caused by nāgas,
diseases caused by yakṣas, diseases caused by asuras,
diseases caused by garuḍas, and diseases caused by gandharvas.
Diseases caused by kumbhāṇḍas, diseases caused by piśācas,
diseases caused by pūtanas, diseases caused by kaṭapūtanas,
diseases caused by vetālas, and diseases caused by rākṣasas.
It completely eliminates all illnesses caused by *karkoṭaka* and *vaitāḍa*,
afflictions brought about by the planets, even cases of poisoning,
as well as all malevolent incantations and the like.
Furthermore, Ānanda, if there is anyone who is ill and recites this secret dharma of the great divine mantra three times daily,
that person’s eyes will attain clarity and see objects as before.
Because this secret great divine mantra of the pure eye possesses such great power,
the eye attains such purity,
removing all darkness as well as internal and external cataracts and obstructions.
Even the obstructions of wind-poison, bile-poison, and phlegm-poison—
all such obstructions as those of phlegm— are entirely eliminated;
there is no pain, no suffering, and no discharge of mucus or tears.
Furthermore, there is the true power of pure precepts, the true power of authentic practice,
the true power of the five supernormal knowledges of the ṛṣis, the true power of the noble ones, and the true power of sacred medicines.
The power of the reality of secret phrases; the power of the reality of dependently arisen phenomena;
the power of the reality of the dharma of suffering; the power of the reality of the dharma of origination;
the power of the reality of the dharma of cessation; and the power of the reality of the dharma of the path.
The true power of the srotāpanna; the true power of the sakṛdāgāmin;
the true power of the anāgāmin; the true power of the arhat;
the true power of the pratyekabuddha; the true power of the bodhisattva; and the true power of the Buddha.
By the power of such truths as these,
the eye attains purity.
At that time, the World-Honored One further spoke this secret mantra:
Namo buddhāya | bhagavato 'stādaśamukha-mahāvidyārājñī svāhā || The Buddha said to Ānanda: "This is a secret and great divine mantra."
If a person recites this together with the aforementioned divine mantra according to the ritual three times each day,
all eye diseases that person possesses will be completely eliminated.
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One,
I shall now, receiving the holy command of the Buddha,
take this secret and great divine mantra and go to the residence of the householder Sukhita to proclaim it extensively."
He brought great benefit to the householder Śubhavyūha and the fourfold assembly.
When the Buddha had finished preaching this sutra, the Venerable Ānanda and the great multitude,
having heard what the Buddha taught, were all greatly rejoiced, and they faithfully accepted and practiced it.
The Sūtra on the Elder Sunanda Spoken by the Buddha
